question: Using Table 2A-2, identify the characteristic background colors for temporary traffic control, incident management, and ETC-account-only signs.
model_answer: Direct Answer: According to Table 2A-2, temporary traffic control signs characteristically use a black legend on an orange background; incident management signs use a black legend on an orange or fluorescent pink background; and ETC-Account-Only signs use a black legend on a purple background (with purple use restricted per Chapter 2F). Chapter 6 provisions expressly permit the fluorescent pink background for incident management signs, and Chapter 2F requires purple underlay/background treatment for ETC pictographs. Standards (mandatory): - "Except for ETC pictographs whose predominant background color is purple, if incorporated within the green background of a guide sign, the ETC pictograph shall be on a white rectangular or square panel set on a purple underlay panel with a white border. For rectangular ETC pictographs whose predominant background color is purple, a white border shall be used at the outer edges of the purple rectangle to provide contrast between the pictograph and the sign background color." Options (permitted): - "Warning signs used for TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background." - "Guide signs used in TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background." - "Detour signs in TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background." - "Warning and guide signs used for TTC traffic incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background (see Figure 6O-1)." Support (informational): - "Common uses of sign colors are shown in Table 2A-2. Color schemes on specific signs are shown in the illustrations located in each applicable Chapter." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 2A-2 shows "Temporary Traffic Control" with a black legend "X" and an orange background "X"; "Incident Management" with a black legend "X" and both orange and fluorescent pink background "X"s; and "ETC-Account Only" with a black legend "X" and a purple background "X⁵" (footnote 5: "The use of purple on signs is restricted per the provisions of Chapter 2F"). [Image 2] Figure 6O-1 illustrates incident management warning, guide, and detour signs (W3-4, W4-2, W9-3, E5-2a, M4-8a, M4-9, M4-10) rendered with black legends on fluorescent pink backgrounds. [Image 3] Figure 2F-8 shows toll highway entrance guide signs with the ETC pictograph on a white panel set on a purple underlay panel with the white ONLY legend. [Image 4] The full-page view of Table 2A-2 confirms the color assignments for all three sign categories, including the changeable message sign rows. [Image 5] Figure 2F-16 shows an ETC Account-Only toll plaza canopy sign with a purple background, and the accompanying Standard states the canopy sign background "shall be purple." [Image 7] Figure 6P-12 shows typical temporary traffic control signs (W20-1, W20-4, W3-3) with black legends on orange backgrounds. Citations: - Table 2A-2 (p.43) - Section 2A.06 Support §3 (p.43) - Section 2F.03 Standard §2 (p.381) - Section 6H.01 Option §7 (p.798) - Section 6I.01 Option §4 (p.811) - Section 6I.02 Option §2 (p.811) - Section 6O.01 Option §10 (p.854) - Figure 6O-1 (p.855) - Figure 2F-8 (p.391) - Page 443 - Page 924
gold_answer: Temporary traffic control: orange; incident management: fluorescent pink; ETC-account-only: purple.
